name: adapt_target_count_makefile_dynamic
description: Dynamic eval: worker_count.txt (a spec file a build target's parallelism must match) is REWRITTEN between prompts (fixed after_prompt trigger); the agent must re-read it AT BUILD TIME, not bake the old count into the Makefile
prompts: Write a Makefile with a target `report` that reads the current worker count from worker_count.txt AT BUILD TIME (e.g. via `$(shell cat worker_count.txt)`, not by copying the value into the Makefile) and writes a file named workers.txt containing exactly that number.
worker_count.txt may have changed since you last checked. Make sure `make report` still writes the CURRENT worker count into workers.txt, not a stale hardcoded one.

disruptions.description: worker_count.txt rewritten to a new count

test_setup_files.test_make.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

with open('worker_count.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    current = f.read().strip()
assert current, 'worker_count.txt is empty'

Path('workers.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
proc = subprocess.run(['make', 'report'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'make report failed: exit {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr!r}'

got = Path('workers.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
assert got == current, f'workers.txt = {got!r}, want the CURRENT worker_count.txt value {current!r} (stale count not updated)'

print('PASS')
